$comment: Green-on-arrival baseline for TRO-244 (assignment rule 4: pnpm audit is one of
the 7 required CI checks). Same pattern as audit/factory/quarantine.json for
test regressions: scripts/factory/lib/dependency-audit-diff.mjs compares
ADVISORY IDENTITIES against this file, not raw vulnerability counts, so a PR
only fails on a NEW advisory it introduces - not on the pre-existing set.
WHY a baseline instead of a hard audit-level gate: pnpm audit --audit-level=high
reported 135 pre-existing findings (10 low / 64 moderate / 58 high / 3 critical)
in the lockfile at original capture time (2026-07-31), none introduced by that
change. A naive 'fail on any finding' step would have redded every PR in flight.
See CHANGES.md (TRO-244) for the full documented-deviation rationale.
Remediating this inherited set is tracked but was explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for
TRO-244 - that work is dependency upgrades/replacements per advisory, not a
CI-pipeline change. This file makes the number visible and non-regressing
instead of unenforced; it does not claim every remaining advisory is fixed.
Identity format: GitHub Security Advisory ID (GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx). Falls back
to 'pnpm-advisory-<numeric id>' for the case (not observed at capture time, but
handled) of an advisory with no GHSA id.
2026-08-03 refresh: 10 NEW advisories had surfaced since 2026-07-31 (undici,
fast-uri, hono, postcss, ip-address, brace-expansion - all transitive, none a
direct dependency) and were blocking the required 'typecheck . build . unit
tests' CI check for unrelated PRs. Fixed via scoped pnpm.overrides in root
package.json pinning each to its minimum patched version per its GHSA advisory
- see that file's adjacent comment. Re-running the audit after the fix also
resolved 49 previously-baselined advisories as a side effect of pnpm's resolver
re-deduping the tree under the new constraints (not deliberately targeted).
Net: 124 -> 75 known advisories. The 49 resolved ids are listed in this
commit's message for auditability; removed from knownAdvisories below per this
file's own refresh procedure so a regression would be caught again.
To refresh after a deliberate dependency bump that resolves some advisories:
run `pnpm audit --json > /tmp/audit-now.json`, then
`node scripts/factory/lib/dependency-audit-diff.mjs --current /tmp/audit-now.json
--baseline audit/factory/dependency-audit-baseline.json` to see exactly which
GHSA ids resolved, then regenerate this file's knownAdvisories/severityCountsAtCapture
from that same audit-now.json and commit it in its own commit naming the ids removed.
Never add an ID here that pnpm audit did not actually report as of the commit
in capturedAtCommit - that would silently widen the baseline instead of
reflecting reality.

severityCountsAtCapture.note: Counts are by finding (advisory x affected dependency path), matching pnpm audit's own human-readable summary line - NOT the same as knownAdvisories.length below, which counts unique GHSA ids. One advisory can affect more than one dependency path, so 75 unique advisories produce 85 findings.
